beliefs: Every character is shifted by ASCII +1 (a→b, A→B, 0→1, space→!, ~→DEL) [E1, E5, E7]
After shifting, a lowercase letter's result is uppercased ONLY if the previous ORIGINAL character is not a lowercase letter (run-start) [E12, E13, E16, E17, E18, E19]
Uppercase letters, digits, spaces, and symbols get only the raw +1 shift with no case change (A→B, Z→[, 0→1) [E1, E2, E7, E11, E17, E19]
The run-start test looks at the original character, not the shifted one, so 'aB'→'Bc' and 'Ba'→'Cb' [E12, E13, E16, E17]
When the run-start char is 'z', its shifted result '{' is uppercased to '[' [E8, E11, E15]
Only the first char of a lowercase run is uppercased; subsequent lowercase letters keep their raw +1 shift, so 'ab'→'Bc', 'aa'→'Bb', 'baa'→'Cbb' [E12, E13, E14, E18]
The 'z'→'[' uppercase exception applies to every run-start 'z', including 'zz'→'[{', 'zzz'→'[{{', 'zzaz'→'[{b{' [E15]
Uppercase letters are NOT lowercased after shifting; they stay as their +1 shifted uppercase/symbol (A→B, Z→[) [E7, E11, E16, E17, E19]
notes: The v18 predict() code was already correct; the discrepancy was only in the prose beliefs, which wrongly said 'previous ORIGINAL character is not lowercase' but the code checked prev_lower correctly. E19 confirms the run-start rule holds across all non-lowercase preceding chars (uppercase, digit, symbol, space). No code change needed.
